purpose: Inspiration for Transit Trinidad pass-through boarding and informal-route UX. These are design references, not Trinidad route evidence.

references.name: GTFS Continuous Stops
references.lesson: Represent pickup/drop-off between stops as explicit segment-level policy instead of inventing dense fake stops.

references.name: GTFS Flexible Services
references.lesson: Separate demand-responsive or flexible access from ordinary scheduled/fixed-route travel.

references.name: OpenTripPlanner Routing Modes
references.lesson: Model walking to a pickup point along a road as a distinct access behavior, not as a normal stop.

references.name: TfL Bus Stop Design Guidance
references.lesson: Hail-and-ride sections should be treated as safety-sensitive and less certain than fixed stops.

references.name: Digital Matatus
references.lesson: Informal transit can be made map-usable through adapted GTFS-style data without pretending it is fully formal.

references.name: Transport for Cairo Greater Cairo Region Digitalization
references.lesson: When exact stops are messy, use surveyed terminals and virtual stops with explicit confidence.

references.name: Trufi Core
references.lesson: Open informal-transport journey planners still need bounded walking distance, candidate limits, and route confidence.

references.name: Trotro App
references.lesson: Door-to-door public transport UX is valuable, but users must also be able to report missing or wrong routes.
